title: declare-ci-stage-weights-and-dep-sanitizer
author: Samira Khan
description: This PR introduces a small declarative manifest for CI stage weights and adds a lightweight dependency sanitizer that trims unused dev-deps during presubmit image builds. Motivation: long presubmit startup times and noisy dependency churn make premerge feedback slow for large surface changes. The change has three objectives: 1) make CI stage selection explicit and data-driven via ci/stages.yaml so teams can assign relative weight and target runners; 2) produce thinner presubmit images by running a dep-sanitizer step that reconciles package manifests against a curated allowlist and a simple reachability check; 3) wire a release-sanitizer hook that annotates release artifacts with a dep-sanity stamp so QA and release automation can gate on dependency hygiene. The description below includes commits, files changed, review thread highlights, CI summary, and merge notes.
commits: init: add declarative ci stages manifest and loader (ci/stages.yaml)
feat(dep-sanitizer): add lightweight sanitizer binary and CLI (tools/dep-sanitizer)
ci: presubmit images: run dep-sanitizer during slim build path (scripts/presubmit/*)
docs: add dep-sanitizer README and migration notes
review_comments: Diego Marquez: Nit: prefer explicit stage priorities as integers instead of floats to avoid rounding inconsistencies in the scheduler. Also can you add a link to the staging runner pool?
Samira Khan: Updated stages.yaml to use integers and added runner_pool field; pushed a follow-up commit. See commit 'ci: use integer stage weights'
Priya Nair: Security concern: dep-sanitizer currently runs a simple reachability check that spawns npm/pip inspect commands inside a builder image. Can we sandbox and timeout the check?
Samira Khan: Added timeout (45s per package) and moved checks into an ephemeral container performed by the existing presubmit runner; added note in README about how to opt out for legacy projects.

Tom Bennett: CI: presubmit pipeline flaked once on integration tests after slimming images; looks like a test relying on a dev-tool binary removed by the sanitizer. Can we add an opt-in allowlist file per-package?
Samira Khan: Added tools/dep-sanitizer/allowlist.txt support and per-project .presubmit-allowlist path; added migration guidance in docs/ci-migration.md
ci_checks: integration-smoke: flaky (1 failed run) -> rerun: pass
release_notes:
- Introduce declarative ci/stages.yaml to control stage weights and runner targeting.
- Add tools/dep-sanitizer: a fast, opt-in sanitizer for presubmit image builds to remove unused dev dependencies and shrink image size.
- Presubmit images now have a slim build path that runs the sanitizer; projects can opt out with .presubmit-allowlist.
- Release artifacts are annotated with a dep-sanity stamp to help release gating and audits.
notes_for_oncall: After merge, monitor presubmit-image-build times and the presubmit queue length for 48 hours. If any team reports missing dev tooling in CI, advise adding entries to .presubmit-allowlist or to tools/dep-sanitizer/allowlist.txt. Watch presubmit failures tagged with 'dep-sanitizer' and revert the commit if wide breakage occurs.
migration_instructions: 1) Add a minimal .presubmit-allowlist at repo root if your build uses non-declared dev tooling. 2) Read docs/ci-migration.md for examples. 3) Teams that rely on legacy monorepo devdeps can opt-out by setting CI_PRESUBMIT_SLIM=false in their pipeline config.
risk_assessment: Medium: changes are isolated to presubmit and release hooks but touch presubmit images and a new binary. Mitigations: opt-out flag, allowlist, and staged rollout via a canary label on teams with large custom toolchains.
qa_steps: 1) Run ./scripts/presubmit/build-slim.sh locally for a sample repo. 2) Verify unit and smoke tests pass in presubmit. 3) Validate that release-sanitizer writes a stamp to release metadata. 4) Exercise opt-out by setting CI_PRESUBMIT_SLIM=false and confirm behavior matches previous build path.
audits: Added lightweight telemetry: counts of packages removed and time spent per repo. Telemetry keys: ci.dep_sanitizer.removed_count and ci.dep_sanitizer.duration_ms.
compatibility_notes: Sanitizer supports npm, pip, and go modules in its first iteration. Yarn, poetry and other package managers will be added incrementally. Per-repo allowlist can override default behavior.
authors_acknowledgements: Thanks to Diego for scheduler feedback, Priya for security reviews, and infra guild for runner pool guidance.
